before.name: InTime Solutions
before.description: Scheduling and workforce management for police, corrections, and 911

competitors.why: Both sell cloud shift scheduling to the same police, sheriff, corrections and dispatch workforce buyer; a scheduling sergeant evaluates one instead of the other.
Vector's scheduling and readiness suite competes directly for the same public safety staffing/scheduling contract InTime bids.

paragraphs: InTime sells scheduling software for public safety agencies, built for police, sheriff departments, fire, corrections, and dispatch. The company says it has helped over 500 public safety agencies manage daily scheduling and operations for over 25 years. The head office is in Vancouver, BC.

Beyond shift coverage, the software handles agency leave requests, timebank management, approvals and vacation scheduling. A court and subpoena module adds court appearances to officer schedules, serves electronic subpoenas and communicates with witnesses. Asset tracking assigns vehicles, radios, laptops and firearms to qualified and trained officers.

Anaheim Police Department began using InTime in 2006, replacing spreadsheets for patrol scheduling. That department reports patrol scheduling time falling from about eight hours per cycle to fifteen minutes. Customer data is hosted by Amazon Web Services.

paragraphs: MSAB builds mobile device forensics software, and XRY lets forensic experts and frontline users recover data from phones while maintaining evidential integrity. XAMN handles the analysis side, searching, filtering and visualizing hundreds of gigabytes of mobile data for use in a judicial setting. XEC manages the operation itself, updating forensic software instantly and reporting on team performance.

The stated buyers are law enforcement agencies that want to speed up investigations and eliminate device backlogs. MSAB also sells screening capability to customs and border security. The company says it has over 4,000 customers worldwide.

MSAB Office is the all-in-one package that installs on any Windows based computer, and MSAB Field is the ruggedized version supplied with a Toughbook computer. The MSAB Kiosk is a turnkey unit that lets users with minimal training process many devices from a fixed location. XRY Pro extracts and decodes data from devices that are locked or encrypted.

quote.text: The .xry file format is forensically secure

provenance.quote: XRY enables both forensic experts and frontline users to recover more critical data in less time, all while maintaining full evidential integrity.

Manage mobile forensics, improve the performance of your team, instantly update forensic software, monitor and report on operations.
They can allow you to speed up investigations, eliminate device backlogs and increase efficiency.
We provide customs and border security with effective screening capabilities.
Trusted by over 4,000 customers worldwide

before.description: Autonomous drones for police DFR programs and public-sector inspection - exhibited at NLC City Summit 2026

competitors.why: 911-response drones staged on police rooftops: same DFR aircraft decision at the same department
DFR software and hardware auto-launching to 911 calls: direct alternative for the same program
Aerodome drone-as-first-responder sold to the same PD launching a DFR program
DFR program software and turnkey operations competing for the same department DFR contract
Autonomous responder drones for first responder situational awareness, same buyer and mission

paragraphs: Skydio makes autonomous drones, along with the docks and software to run them, and sells drone programs to customers from energy networks to neighborhood precincts to battlefields. Those programs cover Drone as First Responder, automated inspection and site security. Dock for X10 positions Skydio X10 drones at a site so that missions launch remotely without anyone present. The smaller Skydio R10 puts eyes indoors before officers enter.

Skydio states that more than 1,500 public safety agencies use its drones. In a Drone as First Responder program, Skydio says its drones launch in under 20 seconds and reach incidents autonomously in under 90 seconds. DFR Command is the software from which remote operators launch and manage drones, respond to multiple calls and stream live video to patrol and command. It integrates with RapidSOS and CAD at dispatch, Axon Fusus for live operations, and automatic evidence upload into Axon Evidence. Skydio's customer stories include Brookhaven PD, which it says reached 30 second response times after deploying 8 Docks.

Skydio Site Security uses the same dock-based drones to verify alarms, patrol perimeters and deliver live visibility across a site. Video streams into Genetec or Milestone, and flights launch automatically when triggered by alarms or access control events. Skydio says its data is encrypted in transit and at rest and that it aligns to SOC 2, ISO 27001 and NIST frameworks.

paragraphs: Ankored automates safety and compliance work for youth sports programs, from background checks on adults through to verification of the players themselves. The company says it brings youth and adult requirements under federal, state and governing body standards into one system.

For clubs and leagues that means automated background checks, training and verification for every coach and volunteer. On the player side it handles age and identity verification. It connects to the sport management tools an organization already runs so coach and player records sit together. Automated reminders and audit ready reports take the place of chasing paperwork.

Parks and recreation departments are one of the named audiences, with staff, volunteer and youth compliance managed across programs, sites and seasons. One case study on the site describes a parks department replacing paper forms with a digital system covering 26 recreation centers. The company's writing points to more than thirty states that now require background checks.

before.name: Anonymous Alerts
before.description: Anonymous student tip reporting and threat management for districts

after.name: Anonymous Alerts
after.description: Anonymous student tip reporting and threat management for districts

paragraphs: Anonymous Alerts sells a reporting platform that gives students, staff and community members a way to raise concerns before they turn into serious incidents. It is used by K-12 schools, districts, colleges and public safety organizations nationwide.

Students can anonymously report bullying, behavioral concerns, threats of violence or mental health risks through a mobile or web interface designed for use across age groups. Designated school administrators receive the information immediately. From a centralized dashboard they can review, manage and investigate reports. Staff can hold real-time conversations with tip submitters while the submitter keeps anonymity. Reporting categories, workflows, notification settings and response protocols can be configured for each organization. A companion panic escalation app lets staff instantly alert administrators and safety personnel.

The company says the system helps schools comply with state laws requiring anonymous reporting systems for school safety and violence prevention. A dedicated page covers Alyssas Law compliance in New York. Newtown Public School District is named on the site as one district that chose the reporting app. The company lists United States patents on the technology, with additional US and non-US patents pending. Anonymous 2-way Communications is registered with the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office.

paragraphs: Anonymous Health sells artificial intelligence software to behavioral health providers, positioned as enterprise class AI for that field. Its central product is described as the world's first AI contact center for behavioral health.

The system handles every call, chat or text on the spot. Intake is automated from paperwork through scheduling. The channels listed are phone, SMS and web chat, running at all hours. Another feature offers real-time coaching to admissions teams at what the site calls the most critical moment of the patient journey. Phone engagement is offered for overflow and overnight calls. During residential stays, interactive programming prepares patients for return to community and for IOP or PHP engagement. Reminder sequences and content programming are used to keep patients engaged. An alumni app is said to support alumni relationships and community referrals.

The site says the company was founded in 2022 by Dr. Angie Chen and other clinical leaders to solve longstanding problems identified in her clinical practice. It describes early work serving thousands of high-risk Medicaid patients. The company claims its automation improves therapist well-being and boosts efficiency by up to 40 percent. Its stated aim is connecting people in recovery with the care they deserve.

paragraphs: Anthropic is an AI safety and research company. It aims to build AI systems that are reliable, interpretable and steerable, and it turns that research into products for businesses, nonprofits and civil society groups.

The company describes a loop of frontier research, safety techniques applied to what it ships, and deployment through partnerships and products. Its models are sold in tiers, with Opus 5 presented as a step change for the Opus tier on coding, agents and professional work. Alongside the models sit purpose-built applications, including Claude Science for researchers.

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation whose stated purpose is the responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity. Governance runs through a board of directors elected by stockholders together with a Long-Term Benefit Trust. Staff are described as researchers, engineers, policy experts and operational leaders drawn from a range of disciplines.

paragraphs: Arly is youth program management software that puts every layer of program operations in one platform. The people who buy it run programs for children, handling enrollment, pricing and payments in the same place.

Families sign up through a customized portal with one log-in, completing forms and uploading documents. Billing and account processing sit alongside, with revenue tracked in real time. Participants are grouped and staff assigned to them for attendance taking and access to health and safety information. Check-in and check-out verifies authorized pick-up contacts in real time. Curriculum is sold alongside the software, one set of it created in partnership with Scholastic. A summer package runs five to six weeks of ninety-minute daily instruction in reading, writing and math. Testimonials on the site are attributed to program staff at YMCA organizations, including the YMCA of Central Virginia. Staff onboarding includes self-paced learning and support from the company's customer experience team.

paragraphs: Automotus sells automated curb management systems to cities and airports. The company says it works with cities, airports and fleets to make communities better places to live.

The cameras attach to existing infrastructure such as streetlight poles. Once installed, the system automates data collection, invoicing and enforcement. Commercial drivers pay for curb time without apps or meters, and agencies can optionally apply discounted rates for electric vehicles. Violations are captured as they occur, with the option of notifying enforcement or issuing a citation automatically. Agencies also receive curb and traffic activity data broken down by every type of vehicle.

The company describes data security and individual privacy as priorities set from the start. paragraphs: The software on this site is sold under the name Neumo, and it handles transactions and interactions between government agencies and the communities they serve. The catalog spans revenue compliance, court management, DMV services and integrated payments.

On the revenue side, the products listed are tax and licensing, short-term rental compliance, auditing and unclaimed property. Court, jury and probation systems sit under the justice line. Public administration covers land records, vitals, records search and pension. A shared platform layer adds reporting and analytics, forms, digital processing, ID verification, eSignatures, alerts and managed IT services.

The company claims 4,500+ state and local agencies across North America as customers. Those buyers are described as city, county, state and federal agencies. One published case study describes how Oregon DMV extended access beyond office hours with self-service kiosks.

paragraphs: Averhealth provides substance use monitoring and treatment solutions. Its work is built around the needs of criminal justice-based substance use monitoring programs.

Samples ship to the company's laboratory in St. Louis the same day, and results come back the next business day after testing. The laboratory is led by a PhD toxicologist. The company states that the lab is CAP-FDT, CLIA, and DEA accredited. Testing covers more than 1,500 substances in urine, oral fluid, hair, and sweat. Its software, Aversys, supports automated, individualized treatment and supervision programs in a paper-free form.

The company describes itself as more than just a drug testing provider. Its stated goal is to support customers as they work to drive sustainable behavioral changes. Averhealth, Avertest, and Aversys are registered trademarks or service marks of Avertest, LLC.

paragraphs: DroneShield sells counter-drone technology, which it calls counter-UAS, to military, government, law enforcement and critical infrastructure operators around the world. The company describes a portfolio that spans RF intelligence, AI, sensor fusion and software. The stated aim is to help customers detect, understand and defeat increasingly complex drone threats. Engineering, manufacturing and support are spread across Australia, the United States and Europe.

One current product, RfRecon, runs on an AI engine called RfAI-3 and detects, classifies and geolocates AIS/ADS-B signals, unencrypted Remote ID beacons and other RF activity across the spectrum. It interoperates with ATAK-CIV, SAPIENT and third-party command-and-control platforms. Deploying several units across distributed sites yields what the company calls network-scale intelligence.
DroneShield was founded in 2014 with a single focus on countering the threat posed by drones. The company began in Virginia in the United States. DroneShield Limited is publicly listed on the ASX.

paragraphs: tip411 provides a web-based toolset that lets a law enforcement agency and the public interact with each other across multiple channels in real time. Each agency gets custom branded iPhone and Android apps that are free for the public to download. The public sends 2-way anonymous tips by text using a custom keyword, by email, through weblinks and through the agency's social media sites. Community alerts go the other way, to the agency's apps, to the public's email or text, and to its social media sites.

The site lists smart tip routing alongside the tips and apps as a headline feature, and states that the platform is FedRAMP Moderate compliant. Agencies featured in the site's news section include the Provincetown Police Department in Massachusetts, with 26 sworn officers, and the Salamanca Police Department in New York, with 17 sworn officers. The Erie County, NY Sheriff's Office, with 173 sworn deputies, and the Kokomo, IN Police Department, with 89 sworn officers, also appear there.

One testimonial, from SGT Kevin Fair, reports a little over 200 tips in the first full year of use and over 4,200 in 2018. Another, from Mayor Rita Ali, counts more than 700 tips since the program started. tip411 plans to show its anonymous tip and community engagement tools at the 2026 Midwest Security and Police Conference.

paragraphs: tip411 provides a web-based toolset that lets a law enforcement agency and the public interact with each other across multiple channels in real time. Each agency gets custom branded iPhone and Android apps that are free for the public to download. The public sends 2-way anonymous tips by text using a custom keyword, by email, through weblinks and through the agency's social media sites. Community alerts go the other way, to the agency's apps, to the public's email or text, and to its social media sites.

The site lists smart tip routing alongside the tips and apps as a headline feature, and states that the platform is FedRAMP Moderate compliant. Agencies featured in the site's news section include the Provincetown Police Department in Massachusetts, with 26 sworn officers, and the Salamanca Police Department in New York, with 17 sworn officers. The Erie County, NY Sheriff's Office, with 173 sworn deputies, and the Kokomo, IN Police Department, with 89 sworn officers, also appear there.

One testimonial, from SGT Kevin Fair, reports a little over 200 tips in the first full year of use and over 4,200 in 2018. Another, from Mayor Rita Ali, counts more than 700 tips since the program started. tip411 plans to show its anonymous tip and community engagement tools at the 2026 Midwest Security and Police Conference.

paragraphs: CCS Health provides training and technology to community-based workforces, organizations and agencies working to improve health outcomes. The work pairs software with a coaching approach that supports clients through transitions of care and builds skills in health management.

The platform offers standard and customizable data collection along with visual reporting of the processes an organization already runs. That reporting lets administrators and analysts follow community data from participant intake through service completion. A referral product, HealthBridge.care, helps community health workers and organizations source referral partners. Training includes coach training and a Community Health Worker Fundamental certified program. The coaching method traces back to 2003, when Dr. Eric Coleman developed the Care Transitions Intervention approach.

Partners named on the site include aging networks, federally qualified health centers, accountable care organizations, community HUBs, and state and county agencies. The company says more than 60 communities nationwide use its solutions. It describes more than 10 years of work in this area. The business began when founder Bob Harnach launched Care Coordination Systems. That company later became CCS Health. It states that partners have earned over $30 million in value-based payments. The care coordination products are described as having earned HITRUST risk-based, two-year certification.

paragraphs: Cumulus sells software that helps community-based care organizations advance whole-person health. Community care hubs, state and regional networks, healthcare partners, and community-based organizations use it to manage referrals, services, programs, partner networks, reporting, and outcomes within one connected platform.

Client intakes are centralized across multiple teams and programs. From there, staff can securely direct referrals, manage client assessments, and track follow-up actions. For community care hubs, the platform handles payer contracts, connects networks of providers, and monitors outcomes. A Veteran Directed Care configuration helps hubs and their partners streamline referrals, centralize veteran documentation, and automate reporting. Another version is tailored to Senior Community Service Employment Program grantees and their subgrantees, covering participant enrollment through performance tracking and payroll.

The platform uses HL7 FHIR standards to bridge gaps between disparate IT systems. The company says it has achieved HITRUST Implemented (e1) Certification. It also states that it works toward ADA and Section 508 accessibility standards.

paragraphs: Transoft Solutions makes software for the people who plan, design and operate transportation systems. Its work spans aviation, civil infrastructure, transportation and operational professionals. On the aviation side that means specialized software to plan, analyze and optimize airport and airspace operations.

The company started in 1991, when co-founder Milton Carrasco developed a vehicle tracking program called AutoTURN. That product grew out of his master's thesis on computerized vehicle-turning simulation. The range has widened since through in-house development and strategic acquisitions. One executive is credited with merging AeroTURN and PathPlanner into AviPLAN.

The company reports more than 100,000 customers in over 150 countries. Clients are described as government agencies at the federal, state, county and municipal levels, along with major international airports and engineering and architectural design firms. paragraphs: Assaia sells software that gives airports, airlines, and ground handlers real-time visibility into aircraft turnaround operations. The problem it names is that missing visibility on the ramp produces costly delays, underutilized capacity, miscommunication, accidents, missed service level agreements, and excess emissions.

Cameras placed across aircraft stands, aerobridges, and the apron generate accurate timestamps for turnaround events in real time. Machine-learning models turn those timestamps into predictions for aircraft off-block and departure readiness. The company says the system can use a wide range of cameras already installed at airports around the world. It runs in the cloud and on premise.

Beyond the core product, SafetyControl detects unsafe situations on the ramp for airports, airlines, and ground handlers. EmissionsControl gives airports real-time monitoring of auxiliary power unit engine usage. A separate interface is designed for airline users, ground handlers, departure coordinators, and gate managers. The company names JFKIAT and Seattle-Tacoma among the airports where its apron product has been deployed. It also states that the solution is fully compliant with the General Data Protection Regulation.

paragraphs: The Weather Company sells weather data, forecasting, and insights to consumers and businesses alike. The industries it names are advertising, aviation, media, and government.

Much of the business runs through a weather data API that customers fold into their own applications, business processes, or custom models. For aviation the pitch is converting complex meteorological data into decision-ready flight and ground insights. The stated aim there is fewer costly delays, better fuel use, and safer crews and passengers from preflight to touchdown. A separate government and defense line is aimed at mission risk from command centers to the tactical edge.

The company traces its work back nearly five decades, combining human meteorological expertise with technology. It also powers a portfolio of three consumer brands used daily around the world. Case studies describe Breeze Airways using its Fusion flight tracking to run more efficiently through major weather events and resume operations faster after disruptions. Another describes NASCAR unifying its weather intelligence with the company to make scheduling and safety calls.

after.name: Frequentis
after.description: Control-room and voice communication systems for airports, ANSPs and public safety

paragraphs: Frequentis supplies communication and information systems for control centres with safety-critical tasks. The work splits between air traffic management, civil and military, and public safety and transport.

On the public safety side the buyers are police, fire brigades, ambulance services, coastguards and port authorities. Voice communication for air traffic control is the anchor, and the company puts its share of that market at around 30%. It also sells aeronautical information management and aeronautical message handling systems. Current development centres on digital remote tower technology, drone management and 5G/LTE in safety-critical applications.

The Austrian company is headquartered in Vienna and was founded in 1947. It keeps a network of branches, subsidiaries and local representatives in more than 50 countries. Around 550 customers in approximately 150 countries rely on its know-how, by its own count. Installed operator positions number around 49,000 worldwide. More than 75% of employees come from science, technology, engineering and mathematics backgrounds.

paragraphs: Doobert is an online software platform custom-built for animal rescuers. Chris and Rachael Roy are named as its founders and owners.

The software is built to help animal welfare organizations streamline foster management, engage volunteers and better care for animals. It grew out of transporting shelter dogs from high-kill locations to areas where they were more likely to be adopted. Developers were hired to put together a system to coordinate those trips. The company calls Doobert the only foster home management solution out there.

Since its launch in May 2014, the company says Doobert has grown to support over 35,000 volunteers and 5,000 organizations across the United States and Canada. Its members are called Dooberteers, who the site says make a difference in the lives of animals every day.

before.name: CareLoop Health
before.description: Smartphone symptom monitoring and relapse-prediction tool for psychosis, sold to mental health services and NHS trusts - exhibited at NatCon 2026

after.name: CareLoop Health
after.description: Smartphone symptom monitoring and relapse-prediction tool for psychosis, sold to mental health services and NHS trusts - exhibited at NatCon 2026

paragraphs: CareLoop Health sells a real-time monitoring and relapse prevention tool for people living with severe mental illness. The company describes a platform that integrates P4 medicine: predictive, preventative, personalised, and participatory.

People using it make daily quick check ins and can draw on a self-management library informed by cognitive behavioural therapy. The system learns a personal baseline in 28 days and then watches for change against it. When something significant shows up, a key worker gets an email notification. Clinical teams work from a real-time panel of their caseload. The company states that early warning signs appear just 3-10 days before relapse.

CareLoop Health says the tool is built on a decade of NHS-led research. Its home page states the approach is validated by five randomised controlled trials. The platform was co-designed with patients, clinicians, researchers and software engineers. Its co-founders hold academic posts, including a professor of health informatics at the University of Manchester. Another co-founder is described as a psychiatrist for over 30 years.

paragraphs: Bamboo Health sells software that joins behavioral and physical health data into a longitudinal patient record and places it inside the systems clinicians already work in. Its audiences include community and behavioral health providers and federally qualified health centers. Accountable care organizations and other provider groups are addressed separately.

Alerts are driven by admission, discharge and transfer feeds, and care navigation can be started from inside an electronic health record. For people with substance use disorder, prescription drug monitoring program data and alerts are used to flag risk and guide patients toward care. Care navigators also review rosters by hand to find high utilizers whose behavioral health needs have gone unmet. Behavioral health referrals and crisis resource availability sit alongside that history in one place.

The company took its present form in 2021, when Appriss Health acquired PatientPing and rebranded. It claims a footprint across 52 states and territories. Encounters on its network are put at 3 billion a year. Published material points to work with the State of Delaware on crisis care and behavioral health coordination.

On the clinical side the site lists SUD providers, detox facilities, hospitals and emergency departments, clinics, FQHCs, and CCBHCs. Payers listed include managed care organizations, Medicaid plans, and commercial insurance.

Connections, the patient-facing app, offers 24/7 access to peer support, meetings, and recovery tools. Published case studies include a county coalition in Hancock County, Ohio expanding its reach through community engagement. In one clinic case study, 83% of new patients using the app were still in treatment against 61% of those not using it.

paragraphs: Greenspace Health builds software for behavioral health care, organized around measuring how the people in treatment are actually doing. paragraphs: CredibleMind partners with health plans, health systems, employers, and communities to break down the barriers of stigma, navigation, and cost that keep people from mental health care. Its platform blends evidence-based self-care, early intervention, and screening-based navigation into one integrated experience.

People start with validated assessments, and each customer configures referral rules and custom questions that triage higher-acuity needs to in-network care. The catalog runs to over a dozen assessments and more than 100 content topic centers. Behind those sit more than 10,000 evidence-rated resources that the company describes as grounded in science. The experience is designed for accessibility and available in 38 languages. APIs and EHR integrations tie the platform into clinical workflows.

The company says it works with more than 150 partners and supports over 40 million lives. Its stated partners include public sector agencies and community organizations. Deryk Van Brunt is a co-founder of the company and serves as its chief executive. Marcos Athanasoulis, also a co-founder, serves as chief technology officer.

quote.text: Our team of designers, data scientists, behaviorists, content creators, and clinicians share a passion for lighting the path to better mental health, for everyone.

paragraphs: Psych Hub sells training and continuing education to behavioral health clinicians and to the organizations that employ them. The catalog runs past a hundred courses spanning the treatment methods, conditions and populations these clinicians work with day to day.

Finishing an eligible course generates a continuing education certificate. Those courses are accredited for continuing education across more than ten bodies. A separate beta tool lets a clinician hold a clinical conversation with an AI client and get feedback on technique against a rubric. Condition specific Clinical Care Pathway certifications are described as still in development rather than available.

Organizations get administrative tooling on top of the library, including assigning and tracking training, building their own branded courses, managing cohorts and roles, and reporting on outcomes. The provider organizations named as buyers are health systems, multi-state groups, CCBHCs and 1099 networks. Separate sections address health plans and payers. Courses are clinically reviewed by a team of licensed mental health experts before publication. An individual clinician can start free, with a paid tier listed at fifteen dollars per seat per month on an annual plan.

More than 70 staff members work on developing, implementing, and supporting healthcare software. The company also states that it achieved Meaningful Use Stage 3 Promoting Interoperability certification. It sells to government buyers as well, describing itself as a managed services firm serving federal, state and local agencies.

paragraphs: Eleos Health builds an AI-powered platform for organizations that deliver community-based care. The company pitches it as a system of action built to prevent denials, closing compliance gaps before revenue is ever at risk. The software spans clinical, compliance, and revenue cycle workflows rather than sitting in a single department.

Real-time suggestions during a session cut the documentation burden carried by providers. Before anything goes out the door, compliance checks flag issues before submission. Automatic scanning of every note is meant to help CQI and audit teams catch risk earlier. An in-workflow clinical co-pilot synthesizes client insights and expert-vetted guidelines for the person delivering care. It integrates with any web-based EHR via a browser extension, which sidesteps custom API work.

The platform is designed for the compliance requirements of organizations that serve Medicaid populations. The company describes enterprise-grade security built for community-based care. Its stated aim is advancing behavioral care through data, measurement, and personalization. Advisors listed on the company page include Dr. David Shulkin, described as Ninth Secretary of US Department of Veterans Affairs.

after.name: HiBoop
after.description: Measurement-based care software that automates validated mental health screenings, scoring and outcome tracking for behavioral health teams - exhibited at NatCon 2026

paragraphs: HiBoop sells an assessment platform for clinicians who practice measurement-based care. Teams use it to automate screening, read scored results before a session, and track what changes between sessions. The stated buyers are clinics, hospitals and private practices.

The library holds more than fifty validated instruments, scored automatically and tracked session to session. Clients receive a secure link by email, SMS or QR code, with no app download or account required. Scoring triggers real-time notifications for critical items, suicide ideation and clinical deterioration. Rather than writing into the chart directly, the platform exports structured clinical data as PDF reports and CSV.

The company states HIPAA and PIPEDA compliance by design, with encryption, signed business associate agreements, role-based access and annual third-party security audits. It says client data is stored in Canada. Every account is described as including a dedicated implementation specialist who walks the team through setup. A published case study describes the Canadian Addiction Treatment Centres moving off paper-based assessment workflows.

before.description: Medicaid enrollment and renewal navigation for states and plans

after.name: Fortuna Health
after.description: Medicaid enrollment and renewal navigation for states and plans

paragraphs: Fortuna Health runs a digital service that helps people apply for and keep Medicaid and other government health coverage. It reaches consumers through providers and insurers rather than being offered directly to the public.

A person starts with a screening rather than a long form, and the site says an eligibility check can take as little as 30 seconds. From there the service guides the person through enrollment and renewal for the Medicaid programs that fit their circumstances. Status notifications follow each important administrative action, so deadlines are less likely to slip past unnoticed. The company states that every one of its navigators is certified and licensed to enroll. Live navigation is offered in more than one language.

Fortuna describes itself as modernizing the infrastructure for Medicaid and government health programs. Case studies on the site include Alomere Health System, described as cutting uncompensated care after working with Fortuna. The company says it is expanding nationwide.

paragraphs: Alivia Analytics sells software and services that help health plans and government agencies cut the losses caused by fraud, waste, abuse and payment errors. Its platform, Alivia 360, gathers pre-payment and post-payment work into one suite.

Before a claim is paid, a claims manager scores high-risk providers and applies configurable pend-and-review triggers with compliance checks. After payment, a lead-finding tool feeds special investigations units while a case manager handles the volume of cases and the workflow around them. A separate data service standardizes claims data into analytics-ready formats and takes in whatever the payer sends. The company frames its AI as an assistant rather than a replacement, with human oversight and ethical use.

Buyers span Medicaid, Medicare and state programs as well as private health plans, third party administrators and self-insured employers. The company says it began by helping state Medicaid programs and Blues organizations speed up post-pay recoveries. paragraphs: HHAeXchange sells homecare software built as one platform connecting providers, payers, and caregivers. Homecare agencies rely on it to be more efficient in their day-to-day operations.

A flexible electronic visit verification system with a GPS mobile app handles caregiver clock-ins and clock-outs. On the revenue side, agencies validate patient pre-authorizations, monitor authorization usage, and stay on top of expirations. paragraphs: Acentra Health builds health technology and clinical services for government healthcare programs. Its Medicaid Enterprise System takes in professional, institutional, and dental claims and encounters, whether they arrive by electronic data interchange or on paper.

paragraphs: Propel makes a mobile app for people who receive government benefits on an EBT card, pitched on its own site as the simplest way to check a balance and save money. The app itself costs nothing to use.

With the cardholder's permission, Propel connects to their state benefits portal. It then gathers the EBT balance and transaction history, makes that easier to read, and displays it in the app. That spares people from calling a 1-800 number or logging in to a state website. Balance checking works in 49 states, the District of Columbia, and several U.S. territories. Iowa is the exception. The app also carries card security features such as suspicious activity monitoring and out of state transaction blocking.

The company says it was founded to make government benefits better at the speed and scale recipients deserve. The company points to more than a million 5-star reviews of the app. Money comes from advertising. Most of the promotions are free or discounted services available only to EBT cardholders. Propel also runs surveys that reach millions of users nationwide. It says those findings give insight to policymakers working to improve state and federal benefits programs.

paragraphs: GetInsured sells software as a service for public sector health care. The company frames the work around a single goal, which is access to affordable coverage for every American. Its implementations run in ten state-based marketplaces around the country.

Consumers use a portal whether they are browsing plans without an account or managing coverage inside one. Someone can start anonymously and then create an account in the same session without re-entering what they already typed. State and support staff work in a separate administration portal showing consumer information, enrollment data and history, ticket history and ticket status. Assisters and navigators get their own portal, where they can see and interact with the Consumer Portal just as the consumer does, including uploading documents for DMIs.

The company names marketplace work in Idaho, Illinois, Minnesota, Nevada, New Jersey, New Mexico, Pennsylvania, Georgia and Virginia. Oregon is described as launching for plan year 2027. It also counts 4.5 million people migrated from Healthcare.gov.

paragraphs: CITIZ3N Government Solutions builds modular platforms for government agencies that oversee Affordable Care Act marketplaces, Medicaid, health and human services programs, and health benefits for government employees. It is a subsidiary of Softheon and one of three brands in that portfolio.

There are two platforms: MARKETPLACE, a set of stand-alone modules meant to integrate into marketplace exchanges for government, and VERIFY, which handles eligibility determinations and combats fraud, waste, and abuse in Medicaid and HHS programs. Both are delivered as cloud-based software as a service. The architecture is cloud-native and uses an enterprise service bus for communication and interoperability between systems. The company says the platforms scale to more than a million transactions per day.

The buyers are local, state, and federal agencies. The company states compliance with HIPAA and regular security audits against frameworks such as NIST 800-53 and MARS-E 2.0. Its annual audits are listed as SOC 1 and 2, PCI AOC, a NACHA audit, penetration testing, vulnerability scanning, and code security scanning. Support is described as implementation assistance, training programs, and ongoing technical help.

after.name: Cayenta

paragraphs: Cayenta makes enterprise software for utilities, covering customer management, billing, financials, work management, and human capital management. Its customers are utilities across the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean.

The customer information system sits at the center, supporting utilities of every size from standard billing through highly complex rate structures. It is built to run the complete meter-to-cash lifecycle inside one system. Work management ties planning, work orders, and cost tracking to that customer and financial data. A financial module handles accounting, budgeting, reporting, and internal controls for utilities and municipalities. An AI layer called Cayla fields customer inquiries across voice and digital channels and answers staff questions inside the application. CayentaCloud provides single-tenant hosting in dedicated environments, and on-premises options remain for utilities not yet ready for the cloud.

The company dates its founding to 1983. It began as Solutions for Government, created to serve the needs of local governments and utilities. Cayenta later joined Harris Computer, which it describes as a global software organization. Its hosting infrastructure carries SOC 2 certification.

quote.text: We proudly serve utilities across the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean.

paragraphs: Adtran builds broadband access equipment and software for service providers that are extending fiber across different technologies and deployment settings. Its access platforms are meant to fit several architectures, from disaggregated designs to integrated systems. The company also sells a pluggable optics module aimed at operators of data centers working under power, cooling, space and latency limits.

Deployments run from small sites carrying a few hundred subscribers up to locations serving more than 100,000. Open APIs and OSS/BSS integration connect the equipment to systems an operator already runs, while the Mosaic software suite supplies visibility from end to end. A shared operational layer correlates signals and alarms across areas that were traditionally kept apart, so a team can see how a fault affects subscriber service before tracing where it began. Fiber monitoring runs while the fiber is in service, looking for degradation before subscribers feel it.

Customer stories on the broadband access page name a rural electric cooperative bringing fiber to parts of Indiana. Another names a municipal power and light utility building a multigigabit fiber-to-the-home network. For buyers who want to talk to someone, the contact page sets out regional office details.

paragraphs: CostQuest Associates is a broadband consulting, data, and technology firm that collaborates with businesses and governments of all sizes. Its work covers network cost, economics, asset valuation, planning, policy, program support, mapping, and data science.

The data side of the business builds broadband-specific geographic information system data and applications for service providers, government entities, engineers, and consultants. It begins by pinpointing Broadband Serviceable Locations at the coordinate and address level across the United States. Essential broadband insights are then layered onto each serviceable location, including service availability, competition, funding details, and cost to serve. A consulting services team builds custom cost, business case, valuation, and appraisal models detailing the economics of broadband infrastructure for service providers, engineers, and governments.

The founders left the corporate telecom world to set out on their own. Over twenty years later, in 2023, the company transitioned to employee ownership. It is headquartered in Cincinnati, Ohio, with a team in Seattle, Washington, and a presence in Washington, D.C. Clients include service providers, engineers, consultants, and governments at the federal, state, and local levels. The company states that it serves as the Broadband Serviceable Location Fabric data provider for the FCC's Broadband Data Collection and for NTIA's BEAD program.

paragraphs: 3-GIS is an enterprise software company whose customers are telecom, electric, and gas organizations that plan, build, manage, and maintain complex infrastructure networks. On the utility side it drives Esri Utility Network workflows with tools for editing, tracing, validation, versioning, map production, and data quality. paragraphs: IQGeo gives telecom and utility operators a single platform to plan, design, build, and operate their physical network infrastructure. It is aimed at telecom, fiber, and utility network operators, including planners, engineers, and construction teams.

Network Manager Telecom is built to plan, build, and operate fiber and coax networks with accurate data, simple field tools, and automated AI quality checks. Field staff can download their work area, update records offline, and sync changes back automatically. Construction photos are audited with real-time visual AI to verify quality, completeness, and compliance at scale. A companion product, Network Manager Electric, is described as built for geospatial work execution, combining geospatial intelligence with AI-powered workflows across the full lifecycle.

Buyers choose between two deployment options, an IQGeo SaaS deployment or a private cloud deployment they host themselves. The hosted option is listed with ISO/IEC 27001:2013 certification. The private cloud option is pitched at operators needing bespoke integration with legacy GIS and OSS/BSS systems. The company says electric and gas utilities rely on it for asset management, grid modernization, inspection and field operations. On the telecom side it describes its customers as reaching some of the largest and fastest-growing global telecom operators, managing highly complex, rapidly scaling networks.

paragraphs: Biarri Networks sells fiber network planning and design, producing construction-ready designs for network operators and engineering teams. The company says its designs arrive up to 25 times faster than traditional methods. Cost estimates and planning insights are aimed at Tier 2 and Tier 3 service providers preparing bids.

The platform is GIS-based and fits its designs into systems and workflows a customer already runs. Plans can be tailored to a customer's own rules, architectures, and deployment environment. Teams can weigh deployment options such as underground against aerial. GIS data can be exported in formats including TAB, SHP, GEOJSON, and KML. Demand forecasting is offered for rural and low-density areas, where operators must justify the build. A standalone software-as-a-service product called FOND Planner lets customers design their own network plans.

The company was founded in Australia to change a traditional and time-consuming planning and design process. Its team now spans Australia, the Philippines, Vietnam, the UK, and the United States, and the Denver office serves as its American headquarters. Its information security management system is certified to ISO/IEC 27001. The company takes part in the Fiber Broadband Association and INCA.

paragraphs: Cambium Networks sells Wi-Fi, broadband and security equipment to organizations building and running their own networks. Named markets include residential broadband and managed Wi-Fi for multifamily buildings, senior living, student housing and affordable housing.

The wireless line runs from Wi-Fi 5 access points through indoor and outdoor Wi-Fi 7 models. Service providers can also offer subscribers a managed home mesh router with cloud visibility and self-service setup. On the wired side, the switches come in indoor and ruggedized versions with Layer 2 and Layer 3 features and Power over Ethernet options for enterprise, industrial and campus sites. Devices are profiled without manual setup, and a switch configures itself as equipment is deployed, disconnected or moved. Management runs from public cloud, private cloud or a customer's own premises. Planning software models a fixed wireless link before anything is bought, weighing geography, distance, antenna height and transmit power.

Customers quoted on the homepage include a technology infrastructure manager at a county public school system. Another is an IT communications manager at a city government. The company courts school buyers directly, promoting a webinar on E-Rate funding.

before.name: Gray Decision Intelligence
before.description: Program Evaluation System analytics on academic program economics, enrollment demand and job outcomes for college and university leadership - exhibited at EDUCAUSE 2026

after.name: Gray Decision Intelligence
after.description: Program Evaluation System analytics on academic program economics, enrollment demand and job outcomes for college and university leadership - exhibited at EDUCAUSE 2026

paragraphs: Gray Decision Intelligence sells analytics software that colleges and universities use to weigh their academic programs. The product is the Program Evaluation System, which the company calls the only complete one for higher education. It is meant to help institutions make decisions that increase revenue, reduce cost and save time.

One part of the system tracks revenue, cost and margin by college, department, program and course. Another reports student demand, competition, wages, skills and jobs across more than 1,500 academic programs and six award levels. Dashboards give a snapshot of program indicators for budget allocation and management. Written reports are generated automatically, distilling more than 50 metrics into short summaries for over 1,500 IPEDS programs. A facilitated workshop puts course data in front of faculty and administrators, who use their own judgment to find efficiencies in the courses and sections offered.

Case studies describe Utah Valley University evaluating program economics down to the course level. Another describes Tiffin University streamlining its review process and reaching 25 percent year-over-year growth in eight programs. A third credits the software with helping Jessup University avoid launching low-demand programs.

quote.text: My message to other universities is that if you are committed to having a process of ongoing program evaluation based on internal and external data analysis, you need Gray PES.

Budget Oversight: Offers a snapshot of KPIs for academic programs for efficient budget allocation and management.
Gray DI provides AI-generated reports that distill over 50 crucial metrics on student demand, job market trends, and competitor activity into concise text reports for over 1,500 IPEDS programs.

Gray DI PES helped Utah Valley University evaluate program economics down to the course level so leadership could respond quickly, minimize disruption, and keep growth moving forward.
Gray DI software and services helped Tiffin University streamline the review process and achieve 25 percent year-over-year growth in eight programs.
With Gray DI’s PES, Jessup University boosted enrollment, avoided launching low-demand programs, and built a data-informed culture that spans recruitment to resource allocation.

after.name: Gravyty
after.description: Alumni engagement, mentoring, student support chatbots, and donor fundraising software for colleges, universities, K-12 schools, and nonprofits - exhibited at EDUCAUSE 2026

paragraphs: Gravyty sells software for alumni engagement, mentoring, career opportunities and community building. The buyers are K-12 schools, nonprofits and higher education institutions raising money. The company describes its aim as rallying a community around a central mission through engagement, giving and stewardship tools.

The products are presented together as integrated solutions to recruit and retain a community. One piece answers student questions across communication channels in multiple languages. Another supplies branded alumni platforms for connection and mentoring, online and off. paragraphs: Foothold Technology sells software for human services agencies, covering case management, client tracking, and treatment planning. The agencies it works with span developmental disabilities, home and community based services, supportive housing, care coordination, and behavioral health.

Billing sits inside the electronic record, so billing for services across an agency runs as a single process. For multi-service agencies it offers a configurable setup for each program. The software is also described as connecting the specialists involved in a client's care. Under HIPAA the company identifies itself as a Business Associate.

Foothold was formed by Marlowe Greenberg, Tom Mitchell and Nick Scharlatt to take software developed at Community Access and make it available to other human services agencies. The company says it now supports hundreds of agencies across the nation, in Guam, and in Puerto Rico. It is a Certified B Corporation and states that it operates to standards of verified social and environmental performance. It also states that it is part of the global Pledge 1% movement, donating 1% of profits. Its timeline notes that Foothold joined Exym and KaleidaCare as part of Alpine Software Group.

paragraphs: Unite Us sells software and data infrastructure for coordinating whole-person care across healthcare, government and community-based organizations. Its named audiences include public health and human services agencies. Managed care and Medicaid plans are also on that list.

The core product is a closed-loop referral system for sending and receiving electronic social care referrals within a network of community partners. Staff can run social needs screenings, after which the platform automatically suggests resources or referrals. A secure chat feature lets users at partner organizations message each other about shared referrals, cases and clients. Integrations let organizations share resources and send referrals without leaving their own system.

Alongside referrals, the company sells predictive analytics meant to predict long-term risks and measure impact. Its Population Insights tool combines social, economic, environmental and health information with modeling to identify at-risk populations. It also automates payments to community-based organizations. The company states that it partnered with Presbyterian Health Plan to create New Mexico's first statewide closed-loop referral system.

paragraphs: Everspot sells cemetery software meant to hold all the tools you need to manage your cemetery in one system. paragraphs: Grave Discover Software sells a web-based cemetery management system that cemetery managers use to maintain burial information and grave locations. The same system lets a cemetery grant the public access to that data along with a searchable map.

Records are digitized into an inventory of burials, occupants, plot owners, deeds, grave types, grave locations and headstone images. The information sits on cloud-based servers that the company says are backed up daily. That is offered in contrast to desktop software, where backups depend on the cemetery's own computer environment. The interactive map can be viewed in four different ways. Public users can search grave occupant information by name, date of birth, date of burial, date of death and type of veteran. A visitor standing in the cemetery can pull the software up on a mobile device through a custom cemetery URL to find the grave they are seeking.

Cemeteries shown on the site include Mica Hill Cemetery, which is located in Durham, CT and operated by Durham Cemetery Company. A cemetery board uses the software to manage one cemetery along with other small cemeteries in its care. The company describes a team made up of designers, developers and usability specialists. It says it aims for software that is user-friendly and affordable.

quote.text: Cemeteries contain decades and sometimes centuries of historical information documenting beloved people; maintaining accurate records is essential.

paragraphs: PlotBox sells software for running cemeteries, crematories and funeral homes. The company pitches it as a way to centralise the key functions of a deathcare operation in one easy-to-use platform.

Mapping tools let staff visualise a cemetery layout, manage plot inventory and track burial locations. Scheduling covers cremations, burials and services across multiple locations. Finance modules handle invoicing, payments, receipts and trust fund management. A public-facing side gives families a search tool for finding the resting places of relatives.

Sean and Leona McAllister founded the company, which combines deathcare management software with georectified mapping. It reports over 130 employees globally. Case studies describe work with Calderdale Council on its bereavement services operations. Another covers Liverpool City Council and its cremation services.

paragraphs: Augintel builds software for health and social services agencies whose staff are buried in paperwork. The product pulls narrative data out of case notes, forms, and records and centralizes it. The pitch is that a worker can review an entire case history in minutes instead of reading the file page by page.

Natural language processing identifies the critical content inside those notes. A case dashboard reveals clinical risks described within notes and maps how those risks progress over the life of the case. Supervisors, quality specialists, and executives can customize a dashboard of quality indicators and alerts across an agency. Frontline staff see risks, strengths, and social determinants surfaced automatically. Alerts for early warning can be customized by the agency.

Caseworkers, clinicians, supervisors, and executives are the intended users. The company describes its team as specialists in natural language processing, a subdiscipline of artificial intelligence that uses computers to understand the written word. Its algorithms were trained with the help of partner agencies to understand the context of social services. Marty Elisco is listed as CEO and chairman of the board.

paragraphs: Casebook PBC sells human services software that covers the work from intake through reporting. It is configurable software built to fit an organization's programs, workflows and reporting requirements.

Teams can standardize intake and assessments. Client data is stored in one system. Reporting starts from templates for common reports, and custom reports can be built for exact needs. Pricing is per user, with flexible plans that let an organization pick the number of users that makes sense for it.

The company describes itself as a public benefit corporation led by a set of core beliefs. It says its SaaS product serves government agencies and nonprofits of all sizes, from intake to case management. Its case studies page says agencies, nonprofits and police departments use Casebook to cut hours of paperwork and turn case notes into proof for funders and boards. The about page notes inclusion in the GovTech 100 list for 2024.
